source_snapshot.procedure: Uses fixed fabric tuple and pcieerror errortype6/7 for Poisoned-TLP TX/RX without a consuming transaction.
source_snapshot.criteria: Calls both correctable and accepts tool PASS plus OS reporting.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic logs cannot prove poison propagation, direction or consumer outcome.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires flag authority, topology, disposable consumer and deterministic AER/application oracle.

old_problem: Command-family-specific errortype6/7 direction and severity are unproven; no transaction actually carries/consumes poison, so neither TX/RX nor application/data integrity can be judged.
disposition_reason: Standard PCIe defines the Poisoned bit but does not define AMD pcieerror flag numbers or which side the tool calls TX/RX. Equal numeric values in einjbiopcie are not authority. A safe transaction can be parameterized only after flag and requester/completer semantics exist. ED-03/15/16 prohibit guessing the stimulus or PASS outcome; Pending/BLOCKED remains.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row67, same-row AI/history2467, endpoint/root-port poison cases and next OCP companion row68.
Preserved every PCIe slot and separate TX/RX Poisoned-TLP coverage.
Required an actual disposable checksum-protected carrier/consumer and requester/completer attribution.
Separated AER reporting from bounded process/I/O/data outcome and recovery.
No NIC installation, traffic poisoning, setting change, retry or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: PCIe Poisoned-TLP TX/RX propagation and consumer handling
test_case.purpose: For each approved PCIe slot, prove separate authoritative TX/RX poison stimuli traverse a disposable transaction, reach the intended consumer, produce the signed AER/application outcome and recover without persistent corruption or fatal escalation.
required_package: Per-slot BDF-to-fabric map and requester/completer roles
Direction-specific AER/source plus process/I/O outcome matrix
OOB device/link recovery and exact restoration runbook
test_case.test_command: Do not run pcieerror 6/7. After approval, baseline one mapped isolated path and disposable transaction, execute one TX stimulus and close its evidence/recovery, then separately execute RX; correlate source/requester/completer, AER status, checksum/application result and restored link/device state.
test_case.expected_result: Each flag affects the intended direction and transaction; the approved consumer outcome and exact AER source/severity occur within timeout; no unintended data modification, fatal/DPC/SyncFlood escalation, host reset or persistent device/link fault remains.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS without authoritative flags and consumer matrix. Tool PASS, generic logs, armed-but-unconsumed poison, wrong direction/source, unexplained data change, fatal escalation or incomplete recovery fails.
safety_gate: Dedicated quiesced endpoint with independent OOB and disposable data only.
One direction and transaction at a time; restore baseline between directions.
Abort on wrong source, unexpected data modification, fatal escalation, reset or link/driver loss.
No automatic retry; preserve transaction and AER evidence.
expected_evidence: Separate TX/RX command and exact AER records
test_case.recovery: Stop injector and transaction, preserve buffers/checksums/AER logs, restore AER/BIOS/HDT state, recover device/link only through the approved path and verify disposable data integrity. Execution stays blocked until all branches are signed.

source_conflict.reason: Direction/severity flags and an observable poison consumer remain undefined.

blocked.reason: Unverified poison commands can corrupt or abort I/O without a deterministic consumer/recovery oracle.
